phase: 9 - production delta audit (independent re-derivation, not a rubber stamp of the prior session's 121-file list)
node01_base_commit_verification: 34f05e8 exists in this repo's own git history (git cat-file -t 34f05e8 => commit), so the changed-file set vs Node01's base was computed directly via `git diff --name-only 34f05e8 HEAD` (784 files) rather than trusting the prior session's reported 767-file figure. The 17-file difference (784-767) is fully accounted for by the WR-CLAUDE-CODE-COUNCIL-PRODUCTION-001/ artifacts directory the prior session committed after it measured its own 767-file diff - confirmed by `git log --oneline 34f05e8..HEAD` and by counting files under that directory in the diff.

methodology.summary: Independent static import-closure trace from the same 4 Council entry points (app/api/chat/route.ts, app/api/chat/execute.ts, app/api/chat/stream/route.ts, app/page.tsx), written as a standalone regex-based Node.js tracer (not reusing any prior session code) that follows both static import/export...from statements AND dynamic import()/require() calls, resolving '@/*' path alias and relative paths with the same extension/index resolution rules as the project's tsconfig. Intersected against the real 784-file changed-vs-Node01-base set to get 'files Council structurally needs AND that are actually different from Node01's base' - the same logical operation the prior session described using in its 'method' field, just re-run independently rather than trusted at face value.
methodology.raw_trace_result: 766 internal files reachable from the 4 entry points with zero unresolved import specifiers (spot-checked; the naive full closure is large - about equal to the full 767/784-file diff - because app/page.tsx is one giant monolithic component that also renders unrelated features like Opportunity Discovery, income-loot, and dozens of Terra/God's Eye layers in the same file; this matches the prior session's own observation that the raw diff and the raw reachable set are both dominated by unrelated accretion).
methodology.verification_of_flagged_items: Specifically re-traced and manually confirmed the two items the mission asked for special attention on: (1) lib/agi-experience/captureFromChatResponse.ts IS a real, unmodified, unavoidable static import in app/api/chat/route.ts as committed, confirmed correctly excluded from Council scope by the prior session, and confirmed the identical presence-on-Node01 risk (untracked lib/agi-experience/ dir of unknown contents) ALSO applies transitively via lib/modular-intelligence/runtimeTrajectoryCapture.ts and experienceHooks.ts, a risk the prior session's needs_verification list did not explicitly capture (see 'audit_findings' below). (2) lib/modular-intelligence/chatTrajectoryObserver.ts and nativeRouterV1Pilot.ts are confirmed genuinely load-bearing, static, unconditional VALUE imports in app/api/chat/execute.ts (lines 71-72) - execute.ts will not build without them - and both are confirmed unmodified/pre-existing (git diff vs their own history shows this branch did not touch them; protected-system-integrity.json's fingerprint match further confirms the whole lib/modular-intelligence/ directory is untouched).

missed_dynamic_imports: components/war-room/council/CouncilDeliberationStream.tsx - real Council deliberation-stream UI, rendered unconditionally in app/page.tsx via next/dynamic(). This is DIRECT_COUNCIL functionality and its absence from the prior delta is a genuine gap, not a stylistic one.

components/war-room/terra/TerraFeatureLayer.tsx - required by TerraShell.tsx and TerraTrafficLayer.tsx (both already correctly in the prior delta) via next/dynamic(). Without it, promoting just the prior 121 files would leave those two files unable to render.

components/war-room/agi-wave1/AgiWaveOnePanel.tsx - rendered unconditionally in app/page.tsx next to CouncilDeliberationStream via next/dynamic(). Same category precedent as lib/opportunity-agents/types.ts already in the prior delta: unrelated feature, but page.tsx will not render without it.
gaps_found_in_prior_121_list.root_cause_of_the_miss: next/dynamic(() => import('...')) calls are dynamic import() expressions, which a purely static 'import ... from' scanner (or a human reading only top-level import statements) would miss. The prior session's own production-delta.json 'method' field does not describe how it handled dynamic imports specifically, and these 3 real gaps are consistent with that step having been skipped or done manually rather than with a tool that follows import().

missed_transitive_dependencies_of_alread.description: chatTrajectoryObserver.ts and nativeRouterV1Pilot.ts were correctly identified as required, but their OWN import chains were not traced further. Both are static, unconditional VALUE imports (not type-only), so their dependencies are real build/runtime requirements, not just typecheck conveniences.
missed_transitive_dependencies_of_alread.significance: Node01 has ZERO files under lib/modular-intelligence/ in its git-tracked base commit (34f05e8), per repo-reconciliation.json. If ONLY the prior session's 121 files (which include just chatTrajectoryObserver.ts and nativeRouterV1Pilot.ts from this directory) were promoted, app/api/chat/execute.ts would fail to build on Node01 - these 15 additional files are genuinely, structurally required, unmodified, frozen Native-Router-adjacent code. This is the most consequential finding of this audit: the prior 121-file delta, if applied literally, would not compile.
missed_transitive_dependencies_of_alread.action_taken_this_session: READ ONLY, for tracing purposes, as explicitly permitted by this mission's hard constraints. None of these files were edited. protected-system-integrity.json confirms the whole lib/modular-intelligence/ directory fingerprint is unchanged from the prior baseline.

widened_needs_verification_scope.description: The prior session flagged exactly one needs_verification_at_promotion_time item: lib/agi-experience/captureFromChatResponse.ts (a DIRECT import of route.ts). This audit found the identical Node01-provenance risk also applies, via a different import path, to 3 more files that the required modular-intelligence chain depends on. These are NOT added to the promote list (consistent with how the prior session treated captureFromChatResponse.ts - excluded from Council scope, deferred to promotion-time verification), but are flagged here so the risk is not silently narrower than it actually is.

over_inclusions_found_in_prior_121_list.description: 4 files in the prior delta are confirmed byte-identical to Node01's base commit (34f05e8) via `git diff` - Node01 already has these exact files, so re-promoting them is a harmless no-op, not a correctness bug, but not necessary for a MINIMUM delta either.

additional_already_present_files_found_w.description: While tracing the newly-found modular-intelligence gap, 3 more reachable files turned up that are also byte-identical to Node01's base commit - these were never in the prior 121 list and do NOT need to be added, because Node01 already has them unchanged.

audit_findings.unrelated_exclude_findings: None. Every file in the prior 121-file list was independently confirmed to be either genuine Council/UI code or a real, traceable compile/render dependency of app/page.tsx or app/api/chat/execute.ts - including the large Terra/God's Eye subsystem, which is co-rendered in the same monolithic app/page.tsx shell and is a real, verified page-render dependency (e.g. TerraShell.tsx and TerraTrafficLayer.tsx both dynamically import TerraFeatureLayer.tsx, confirming the whole Terra chain is load-bearing for page.tsx, not decorative). Nothing was reclassified UNRELATED_EXCLUDE.

overall_verdict: The prior session's 121-file candidate delta was a good-faith, mostly-correct first pass, but this independent audit found it was NOT actually complete: applied literally, it would have failed to compile on Node01 because of the missing modular-intelligence transitive chain and the 3 dynamic-import UI files. This audit's minimum, independently-verified production delta is 135 files. The prior session's own explicit caution ('CANDIDATE - not yet applied to Node01') and Commander-checkpoint stop before touching Node01 meant this gap was never actually exercised against production, so no harm occurred - but it is exactly the kind of gap this cloud final-gate audit exists to catch before a real promotion.
